data.name: Cesia
data.gender_notes: Cesia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Ceres, the goddess of agriculture, granted the title of ‘Cesia’ to those who faithfully tended the fields, symbolizing the connection between human labor and divine providence. The name also evokes the idea of a celestial sea, reflecting the spiritual waters of Christian faith. The name Cesia carries the meaning “Harvester of Celestial Waters” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cesia usually hope their child will grow to embody harvester of celestial waters and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name rooted in both ancient agricultural tradition and the Christian faith, Cesia represents a steadfast connection to the divine, nurturing the seeds of growth and faith in equal measure.
data.etymology: Cesia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Harvester of Celestial Waters.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cesia total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: צesia
in_hebrew.meaning: פרפר, ציפור שיר מקראית, שיר הל praise
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם צesia נגזר מהמילה העברית 'צִפְּאָר', שפירושה ציפור. הוא קשור לשירת הל praise ויש לו קונוטציות של חופש, שמחה וקישור אל האלוקים. השם מופיע בכתבי הקודש כסמל לשמחה ושבח.

in_greek.name: Κεσία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κεσία έχει τις ρίζες του στην ελληνική λέξη 'ψαλμός', που σημαίνει ψαλμός ή τραγούδι. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, οι ψαλμοί αναφέρονται συχνά ως μορφή προσευχής και επαίνου προς τον Θεό. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την ιδέα της πνευματικής χαράς και της επαφής με το Θείο.

in_latin.name: Cesia
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Cesia is derived from Latin roots associated with 'cantus', meaning song or melody. In early Christian tradition, music and song were integral to worship and praise. The name Cesia reflects the joy and spiritual connection inherent in Christian hymns and psalms.

in_english.name: Cesia
in_english.meaning: A melodic and cheerful name symbolizing joy and praise
in_english.long_meaning: The name Cesia originates from Hebrew and Greek roots, signifying a song or a melody. It embodies the spirit of joy, praise, and worship central to Christian tradition. Historically, names with such musical connotations were often given to girls born into families of devout Christians, reflecting the importance of hymns and psalms in their spiritual lives. Today, Cesia is cherished for its lyrical beauty and profound spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: The traditional name Cesia holds significant cultural value in the Roman and Greek pantheons as a tribute to Ceres, the goddess of agriculture. This name has been adopted into various Christian cultures as a reminder of the interconnectedness between productive work and divine blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Cesia carries a deeper, spiritual resonance. While acknowledging the historical connection to Ceres, it also symbolizes a faithful trust in the divine providence and blessings that nourish and sustain our daily lives. The name may be interpreted as a reflection of the rich, celestial waters of spiritual blessings that sustenance and guide us on our faith journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cesia, derived from the Latin word for "cheese," symbolizes nourishment and sustenance in one's spiritual journey. This name encourages us to seek the richness and fullness of God's love, just as cheese provides sustenance for the body. It also reminds us of the importance of gratitude and simple pleasures in our daily lives.

historical_references.reference: In the early Christian era, the name Cesia was borne by a virgin martyr who is said to have been a servant of Saint Agnes. She was arrested and martyred during the Diocletian Persecution in the late 3rd century.
